draftPackage.topic: FLIP floating laboratory and ocean measurement
draftPackage.centralQuestion: Why would scientists intentionally tip a floating laboratory upright?
draftPackage.thesis: Controlled rotation changed the platform geometry to reduce wave response and improve a scientific reference, without eliminating ocean motion.
draftPackage.viewerPayoff: Understand why an extraordinary-looking laboratory was shaped to distinguish ocean behavior from instrument motion.

draftAsset.editorialPurpose: Understand why an extraordinary-looking laboratory was shaped to distinguish ocean behavior from instrument motion.
draftAsset.storyAngle: An apparently sinking laboratory deliberately changes shape in relation to the waves to become a better scientific reference.

segments.text: Scientists deliberately tipped this floating laboratory upright. Why?
Because when your instrument moves, it’s harder to tell what the ocean is doing.
FLIP was built to study underwater sound. Even a research submarine turned enough to limit those measurements.
So engineers made a laboratory that travelled horizontally, then flooded ballast tanks to lower its stern.
The lab stayed above water, while about ninety metres of hull extended beneath it.
Look at the shape: a narrow section near the surface, with a broader hull deep below.
In deep water, the motion caused by surface waves weakens with depth.
FLIP’s shape made it much less responsive to those waves.
It could still drift and tilt. Stable didn’t mean motionless.
And when the work was done, compressed air pushed water out of the ballast tanks, returning it to horizontal.
They tipped the laboratory upright to make a moving ocean easier to measure.

misconceptionSafeguards: FLIP is a deliberately rotated spar buoy; no accidental ship sinking or propulsion.
Acoustic reference problem is the initial specific purpose; narration opens with a bounded general explanation, not a claim that moving instruments cannot measure.
Flooding controlled by crew and several tanks; diagrams never present a replication procedure.
Wave-motion attenuation is deep-water surface-wave behavior; no hard cutoff or motionless deep ocean.
Narrow upper / broader deep geometry and large draft reduce wave responsiveness; no universal quantified performance guarantee.
Stable is explicitly qualified by drift and tilt; moored and free-drift research are distinct.
Compressed air expels water for horizontal return, not the downward flip.
Original1963/1997 articles located but bodies inaccessible; no fabricated inspection. Launch-day conflict excluded.
No present-service, current ownership or refit completion assertion.
review.comprehensionReview: Cold viewer sees deliberate upright laboratory before explanatory setup. Moving sensor/reference dilemma supplies why. Same hull changes through transit, ballast, deep shape, waves and residual motion. Final sentence resolves orientation as a measurement tool. The schematic wave overlay supports only qualitative understanding; no resonance formula needed for this short explanation.
review.rightsReview: Original diagrams are the selected visual medium. Scripps brochure diagram and scholarly figures are consultation-only, not cleared or selected production assets. Established licensed Manrope and af_heart are planned, not newly generated. No asset-license entry needed for a research-only reference; record actual future production assets when created.

careAssessment.rationale: Historical engineering explanation with sufficient primary operator and actual field-study evidence; excluded date conflict and unsupported absolute claims do not affect premise. No new services, costs, brand deviation or rights exception.
